entries.answer:
GPT5.6 Sol is a real, newly released OpenAI model (launched July 9, 2026), and yes — you can access it through Requesty's OpenAIcompatible router, though there are a couple of practical fixes needed to your snippet.[1][2]

 Why Your Snippet Needs Adjustment

Requesty exposes an OpenAIcompatible endpoint at router.requesty.ai/v1, meaning you use the standard openai Python SDK but point base_url at Requesty and authenticate with your Requesty API key, not an OpenAI key. Model names on Requesty are prefixed with the provider, so gpt-5.6-sol becomes openai/gpt-5.6-sol, which your snippet already has correct. The reasoning effort parameter (mode/effort) you used in the curl example belongs to OpenAI's newer responses API syntax, not the chat.completions endpoint — Requesty's chat completions passthrough accepts extra OpenAIspecific fields via extra_body, so reasoning_effort needs to go there rather than as a toplevel curlstyle object.[3][4][5][6][7][1]

 Working Python Integration

python
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key="YOUR_REQUESTY_API_KEY",
    base_url="https://router.requesty.ai/v1",
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-5.6-sol",
    messages=[
        {"role": "user", "content": "Explain quantum computing in one paragraph."}
    ],
    extra_body={
        "reasoning_effort": "max"
    }
)

print(response.choices[0].message.content)


This keeps the SDK call pattern you already had, just replaces the invalid toplevel reasoning dict with the extra_body mechanism the OpenAI Python SDK provides specifically for passing nonstandard/providerspecific parameters through to the underlying API. Since GPT5.6 Sol supports a max reasoning effort tier natively (alongside pro as a separate quality mode), you can also try "reasoning_effort": "high" if max isn't yet whitelisted on Requesty's routing layer for your account tier — check Requesty's models endpoint for the exact accepted values for this specific model.[8][5][9]

 Curl Equivalent

If you specifically want to use Requesty's endpoint via curl with the chat/completions path instead of OpenAI's newer responses endpoint (which Requesty does not mirror), it would look like this:

bash
curl https://router.requesty.ai/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REQUESTY_API_KEY" \
  -d '{
    "model": "openai/gpt-5.6-sol",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "user", "content": "Explain quantum computing in one paragraph."}
    ],
    "reasoning_effort": "max"
  }'


Note that Requesty's gateway is built around the chat/completions schema rather than OpenAI's separate responses endpoint, so the original curl structure you drafted (with a nested reasoning: {mode, effort} object and no messages array) won't work against Requesty even though it's valid against OpenAI's own api.openai.com/v1/responses endpoint directly. If you want to hit OpenAI's native responses API with mode/effort reasoning controls exactly as originally written, you'd need to call api.openai.com directly with your actual OpenAI key rather than routing through Requesty, since Requesty currently proxies the completionsstyle interface, not the newer responses schema.[4][5][6]
